🗞 BEAT THE STREET BULLETIN 🗞
Date: 13 August 2026
Telegram: [https://t.me/BeatTheStreetnews]

* 📍 ORDER WIN

LARSEN & TOUBRO: Secures ₹10,000–15,000 Cr mega order to build India’s largest NVIDIA B300 AI Factory for Together AI with 10,000 GPUs at its Chennai data-centre campus.

ASHOKA BUILDCON: Wins AIS transmission project with ₹126.54 Cr annual transmission charges for 35 years to establish the 400/220/132 kV Sakoli substation in Maharashtra.

AURIONPRO SOLUTIONS: Wins ₹100 Cr order from a global hyperscaler to build and project-manage an AI-ready data centre in Navi Mumbai.

OSWAL PUMPS: Wins ₹78 Cr rooftop solar installation order from NBPDCL for 20 MW capacity across 18,089 consumer sites, with additional ₹67 Cr 10-year energy-supply potential.

RAILTEL: Secures ₹63 Cr order from Deendayal Port Authority for an Integrated Gate Automation System at Kandla, including five years of O&M.

SOLEX ENERGY: Wins ₹42.47 Cr domestic order for supply of N-Type TOPCon 620Wp solar PV modules, scheduled for execution in October 2026.

SHARIKA ENTERPRISES: Secures ₹10.42 Cr PEDA order for design, supply, installation and commissioning of LED-based solar street-lighting systems across Punjab.

MAGELLANIC CLOUD: Subsidiary Provigil Surveillance wins ₹3.73 Cr DFCCIL order for E-Surveillance System installation and five-year O&M on the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor.

RMC SWITCHGEARS: Wins ₹1.89 Cr order from Anand Transformers for supply of Transformer Distribution Boxes and turnkey service-connection infrastructure.

* 📍 ACQUISITION

NEPHROCARE HEALTH SERVICES: Acquires dialysis-centre assets in Davao City, Philippines for PHP 71.8 Mn to expand NephroPlus’ international dialysis network.

PANORAMA STUDIOS: Acquires a 10% stake in Rhea & Dia Enterprises through fresh equity allotment as a strategic investment.

ZUARI INDUSTRIES: Approves acquisition of up to ₹150 Cr of Texmaco Infrastructure & Holdings shares and ₹30 of Zuari Agro Chemicals shares from wholly owned group entities.

* 📍 COLLABORATION

GENPHARMASEC: Signs three-year non-exclusive Super Stockist agreement with Amneal Healthcare, with minimum annual sales commitment of ~₹75 Cr, implying ~₹225 Cr over the term.

BHEL: Signs strategic collaboration agreement with Norway’s Hystar for phased indigenisation and local manufacturing of PEM electrolysers for green-hydrogen projects.

RECODE STUDIOS: Opens its first NewU modern-trade store with H&B Stores and plans 15–20 additional stores across high-potential markets over the next 12 months.

TATA MOTORS: JLR and Stellantis sign an MoU to explore new Defender products specifically for the US market.

* 📍 LEADERSHIP CHANGES

TATA CHEMICALS / TATA INVESTMENT: N Chandrasekaran’s reported resignation adds uncertainty to SP Group’s Tata Sons stake monetisation discussions and could delay a potential settlement.

* 📍 NEW PROJECTS

MAX HEALTHCARE: Approves ₹425 Cr expansion at Max Super Speciality Hospital, Vaishali, adding around 250 beds with commissioning targeted by November 2029.

JEENA SIKHO LIFECARE: Plans a new 40+ bed Ayurvedic, Naturopathy & Panchkarma hospital in Bareilly with ~₹85 lakh investment and operations expected from November 2026.

MAGNA ELECTRO CASTINGS: Approves ₹17 Cr investment for a new in-house machining division at its Coimbatore South Campus with seven CNC machines.

STOVE KRAFT: Establishes a China WOS with CNY 10 Mn investment and forms a 50:50 JV to manufacture triply sheets/circles for cookware and other products.

* 📍 FUNDRAISING

SHALIMAR PAINTS: Board approves ₹105.86 Cr preferential issue at ₹85/share involving 1.25 Cr equity shares to three investors.

* 📍 FII STAKE CHANGES / BOUGHT-SOLD

WAAREE ENERGIES: UltraTech Cement agrees to invest ₹27.76 Cr for a 26% stake in renewable-energy SPV Solaris Horizon Energy, with power to be supplied to UltraTech.

* 📍 USFDA / REGULATORY

MISHRA DHATU NIGAM: Becomes the first Indian company to secure GE Aerospace’s S400 approval for independent international metallic-material testing, strengthening its aerospace credentials.

FUSION FINANCE: Clarifies its planned individual-loan product and ₹10,000 Cr AUM target were already disclosed, stating there is no undisclosed material information behind recent stock movement.

ATLANTA ELECTRICALS: SBPDCL withdraws its April 2026 debarment order with immediate effect after considering the company’s appeal and submissions.

* 📍 LAUNCHES

HDFC AMC: To resume lumpsum subscriptions in HDFC Gold ETF and Gold ETF Fund of Fund from August 14 after June restrictions.

* 📍 INCORPORATE / CORPORATE STRUCTURE

STOVE KRAFT: Incorporates Guangzhou Jiawo Import & Export Co. Ltd. as a wholly owned subsidiary in China and forms a 50:50 JV for triply-sheet manufacturing.

MAGNA ELECTRO CASTINGS: Board gives in-principle approval to merge Samrajyaa Precision Machining with the company to bring machining capabilities in-house, subject to regulatory approvals.

* 📍 IT NEWS

LENSKART: Q1 revenue rises 33.6% to ₹2,714 Cr, EBITDA jumps 61.3% to ₹589 Cr and PAT surges 182.3% to ₹228 Cr, with 132 net new stores added.

* 📍 TAX ORDER

* 📍 ADDITIONS

SOLEX ENERGY: Successfully lists on BSE and unveils Vision 2030 targeting 10 GW each of solar module and cell capacity plus 10 GW BESS infrastructure.

* 📍 OTHERS

TATA MOTORS: Q1 consolidated revenue grows 9.3% to ₹95,799 Cr, while domestic PV revenue surges 64.8%; JLR revenue falls 9.6% amid supply constraints and higher incentives.

FINOLEX CABLES: Expects robust communication-cable demand for two years, targets double-digit FY27 margins and plans ~₹300 Cr FY27 capex including accelerated fibre capacity expansion.

JUBILANT FOODWORKS: Maintains 5–7% FY27 Domino’s LFL growth and ~200 bps EBITDA margin expansion target, with Q2 trends starting better than Q1.

MAHARASHTRA APEX: Enters Paulownia/Kiri timber marketing and distribution in India as channel partner for WGW Agreen, targeting timber traders and furniture manufacturers.

V2 RETAIL: Q1 revenue grows 58% YoY with 56 net store additions taking the network to 381, subsequently crossing the 400-store milestone.

INSOLATION ENERGY: Q1 revenue surges 105.37% to ₹745.40 Cr, EBITDA rises 32.97% to ₹76.87 Cr and ₹1,500 Cr FY27 capex is planned for backward integration and capacity expansion.

KRN HEAT EXCHANGER: Q1 revenue grows 119% YoY, with overseas revenue jumping 177.31% to ₹52.38 Cr and domestic revenue rising 107.42%.

MAX HEALTHCARE: Q1 gross revenue rises 16% to ₹2,982 Cr and operating EBITDA increases 15% to ₹704 Cr, while capacity rises to 5,379 beds and Kalinga Hospital acquisition adds 250 beds.

PAGE INDUSTRIES: Q1 revenue grows 7.9% YoY as management remains positive on consumer demand, new products and gradual production-capacity ramp-up.

HINDUSTAN OIL: Begins compressor testing in a revised Block B-80 MOPU configuration allowing lower suction pressures, with partial gas sales underway.

KIRLOSKAR ELECTRIC: Q1 order booking rises 28% YoY to ₹184 Cr, but revenue falls 21% due to subdued billing and customer-delayed dispatches.

INDO COUNT INDUSTRIES: Maintains ₹5,500 Cr FY27 revenue and ~13% EBITDA margin guidance, with core volumes targeted at 105–110 Mn metres.

JINDAL STAINLESS: FY26 revenue reaches ₹42,955 Cr and EBITDA rises 19.2% to ₹5,560 Cr after commissioning a 1.2 MTPA Indonesian melt shop.

DMCC SPECIALITY: Q1 profit growth benefits significantly from sulphur-related inventory gains, while management expects earnings to normalise as prices moderate.

LINCOLN PHARMACEUTICALS: Expands global footprint with 600+ formulations, exports to 60+ countries and manufacturing facilities in Gujarat supported by international certifications.

IMAGICAAWORLD ENTERTAINMENT: Wins arbitration case involving land parcels, with the claim for specific performance dismissed and no financial liability expected.

JNK INDIA: Maintains 20–25% FY27 revenue growth and 12–14% EBITDA margin guidance, backed by ₹1,801 Cr order book and ₹6,000 Cr+ bid pipeline.

K.P. ENERGY: Guides for 30–40% FY27 revenue growth while prioritising execution of the existing order book and selective new orders.

FLAIR WRITING: Retains 15% FY27 revenue-growth guidance and targets 17.5–18% EBITDA margin through capacity utilisation, pricing and cost efficiencies.

PI INDUSTRIES: Maintains low single-digit FY27 growth guidance and ~24% EBITDA margin, with ₹700–800 Cr capex focused on manufacturing, Pharma, Electronics and innovation.

SAI PARENTERALS: Retains ₹750 Cr FY27 revenue guidance and ~17% EBITDA margin target, supported by margin recovery, acquisitions and injectable-capacity expansion.

CALIBER MINING & LOGISTICS: Targets 45–50% FY27 revenue growth and 35%+ EBITDA/PAT growth, with stronger execution expected after the monsoon.

ASHIANA HOUSING: Maintains ₹2,100–2,200 Cr FY27 presales guidance and targets 20%+ ROE, while building a ₹10,000 Cr Senior Living project pipeline.

SEQUENT SCIENTIFIC: Targets 13–15% annual growth over the next two years and 20–22% EBITDA margins, with ₹250–300 Cr FY27 capex for manufacturing and R&D expansion.

INDO FARM EQUIPMENT: Maintains 20–25% FY27 revenue growth guidance, with tractor growth targeted at 25–30% and crane growth at 15–20%.

AIA ENGINEERING: Retains 20–22% operating-margin guidance while sharply raising FY27 capex to ₹350–400 Cr, including ₹170–200 Cr for a new corporate house.

KAMAT HOTELS: Plans to add around 400 hotel keys over 12–15 months and targets ~30% EBITDA margin over the next 2–3 years.

SADHAV SHIPPING: Retains 20%+ FY27 revenue-growth guidance, with profit expected to grow faster as resource utilisation improves.

GUJARAT GAS: Targets 12–13% CNG volume growth, maintains ₹1,100 Cr FY27 trading-profit guidance and plans ₹1,000 Cr CGD capex.

MAN INDUSTRIES: Targets ~₹5,000 Cr FY27 revenue and expects 25–35% annual growth from FY28, supported by Saudi expansion, NPC and Jammu stainless-steel capacity.

ISGEC HEAVY ENGINEERING: Targets 11–15% FY27 standalone revenue growth, with project EBIT margins expected to improve gradually and a new Services division planned.

GRASIM: Birla Opus targets 50%+ FY27 revenue growth and ₹10,000 Cr revenue by FY28, while Birla Pivot targets EBITDA break-even by FY27-end.

GUJARAT FLUOROCHEMICALS: Targets 17–20% fluoropolymer growth, with battery materials expected to reach ₹100 Cr+ quarterly revenue run-rate by Q4 FY27.

ASTRAL: Retains double-digit FY27 plumbing-volume growth and 20–25% paints revenue-growth guidance, with management confident of exceeding the paints target.

CAPLIN POINT LABORATORIES: Expects the US business to become a major growth driver, with expansion focused on the US, Mexico and Brazil and new manufacturing lines ramping over the next 1.5–3 years.

APOLLO HOSPITALS: Q1 consolidated revenue rises 21% to ₹7,043 Cr, EBITDA increases 28% to ₹1,092 Cr and PAT grows 34% to ₹581 Cr, with 5,800+ beds planned over five years.

SOMANY CERAMICS: Targets 12%+ EBITDA margin, with debottlenecking and new southern capacity expected to add significant revenue potential through FY28.

ZIM LABORATORIES: Targets 10–15% FY27 revenue growth and expects 30–35% FY28 growth after EU-GMP certification and commencement of EU supplies.

LENSKART: Management sees significant long-term runway from India’s untapped eyewear market, international expansion, manufacturing scale-up and technology-led innovations including Self-I-test and smart glasses.

HAL: Defence Ministry issues ~₹1 lakh Cr RFP for 60 multirole transport aircraft to replace ageing An-32s, creating a major opportunity for HAL and other Indian partners.

GMR AIRPORTS: Q1 Delhi Airport passenger traffic rises 6.9% to 20.4 Mn with EBITDA up 10.8%, while Hyderabad and Goa traffic decline amid geopolitical and airline-route challenges.

• 🌍 Amneal Pharmaceuticals is a NASDAQ-listed global pharmaceutical company with a significant manufacturing presence in India.

Tata Motors PV | Q1FY27 Results

Financial Performance
- Net Profit: ₹859 Cr (-79% YoY | -85% QoQ).
- Revenue: ₹95,799 Cr (+9% YoY | -9% QoQ).
- EBITDA: ₹6,176 Cr (-24% YoY | -45% QoQ).
- EBITDA Margin: 6.5% (vs 9.3% YoY | 10.7% QoQ).

Results Vs Estimates
- Revenue: ₹95,799 Cr vs ₹93,072 Cr estimate.
- Revenue beat estimates by 2.9%.
- EBITDA: ₹6,176 Cr vs ₹6,867 Cr estimate.
- EBITDA missed estimates by 10.1%.
- EBITDA Margin missed by 90 bps.
- Revenue beat, profitability missed.

Domestic PV Business
- Domestic PV Revenue: ₹17,930 Cr.
- Domestic PV Revenue Growth: +65% YoY.
- Domestic demand remains healthy.
- EV penetration continues increasing.
- New launches support growth outlook.
- Supply debottlenecking remains focus.

JLR Performance
- JLR Revenue: £5.97 Bn (-10% YoY).
- Wholesale Volumes: -9.2% YoY.
- Adjusted EBIT Margin: 2.8%.
- EBIT Margin declined from 4.0%.
- JLR EBITDA Margin: 8.1%.
- PBT: £109 Mn (-69% YoY).
- PAT: £66 Mn.
- FCF remained negative at £998 Mn.
- Supply constraints impacted performance.
- Middle East disruption affected volumes.
- Jaguar model wind-down impacted volumes.

JLR Product Outlook
- Four new BEV products launching soon.
- Range Rover mix remains strong.
- Range Rover Sport and Defender mix: 80.8%.
- JLR targets double-digit revenue growth.
- Target period: Next five years.
- Cost savings target: £1.7 Bn.
- Savings targeted over two years.
- JLR-Stellantis MoU explores Defender products.
- Focus includes US market opportunity.

Balance Sheet
- Net Debt: ₹42,200 Cr.
- Free Cash Flow: -₹11,800 Cr.
- Negative FCF remains key concern.
- Balance-sheet deleveraging requires monitoring.

Management Outlook
- Domestic demand expected to remain healthy.
- EV penetration remains supportive.
- New launches expected to drive growth.
- Revenue growth remains key focus.
- Cost reduction initiatives continue.
- Calibrated pricing actions planned.
- Supply constraints targeted for resolution.
- Commodity costs expected to remain elevated.

Key Positives
- Domestic PV revenue grew 65%.
- Healthy domestic demand environment.
- Rising EV penetration supports growth.
- New launches provide growth potential.
- Strong premium JLR product mix.
- Four new BEVs expected.
- Significant JLR cost-saving opportunity.

Key Concerns
- Sharp PAT decline.
- EBITDA margin compressed significantly.
- JLR revenue declined 10%.
- JLR profitability weakened.
- Negative consolidated FCF.
- Net debt remains elevated.
- Commodity costs remain high.
- Geopolitical risks persist.
- Supply constraints remain monitorable.

Key Monitorables
- Domestic PV volumes.
- EV penetration.
- New model launches.
- JLR BEV launches.
- JLR wholesale volumes.
- JLR EBIT margin.
- Supply-chain normalisation.
- Commodity cost trajectory.
- FCF improvement.
- Net debt reduction.
- JLR cost savings.

Impact
- Mixed to Negative.
- Domestic PV performance remains strong.
- Consolidated profitability weakened sharply.
- JLR remains the major drag.
- Margin recovery is critical.
- New launches provide medium-term upside.

Key Takeaway
- Tata Motors PV delivered a mixed Q1FY27, with domestic PV revenue growing strongly by 65% but consolidated profitability declining sharply due to weaker JLR performance, supply disruptions, geopolitical issues and elevated costs. Revenue beat estimates, while EBITDA and margins missed expectations. Healthy domestic demand, rising EV penetration and upcoming JLR BEV launches provide growth opportunities, but margin recovery, FCF improvement, JLR execution and debt reduction remain the key monitorables.

• 🎯 JLR targets double-digit revenue growth over the next 5 years and expects £1.7 bn cost savings over 2 years.

Unihealth Hospitals achieves another clinical milestone in Advanced Minimally Invasive Surgery

Unihealth Hospitals Limited (NSE Emerge: UNIHEALTH) announces that UMC Hospitals, Navi Mumbai, has successfully treated a 33-year-old patient with a large walled-off pancreatic necrosis, a serious delayed complication following severe pancreatitis.

The complex case was successfully managed by Dr. Harsh Sheth, Consultant Bariatric & GI Laparoscopic Surgeon, using an advanced laparoscopic minimally invasive approach, avoiding the need for a conventional large open surgery. 

This achievement further strengthens UMC Hospitals, Navi Mumbai’s capabilities in Gastrointestinal, Laparoscopic and Pancreatic Surgery, and adds to its growing portfolio of advanced clinical interventions.

In recent months, UMC Hospitals has achieved several notable milestones, including Robotic Knee Replacement, IVUS-guided Cardiac Intervention and Navi Mumbai’s 1st Bilateral Robotic Direct Anterior Approach Total Hip Replacement.

Business Overview
- Nuts and dry-fruits business since 2014.

Capacity Expansion

- Q2 and Q3 require close tracking.

Melt n Mellow
- Acquired regional Maharashtra ice-cream brand.
- Business transformed after acquisition.
- 189+ SKUs.
- 34,000+ retail outlets.
- Q1FY27 Growth: 230%.
- Ice-cream segment is key growth driver.

Distribution Expansion
- FY26 Deep Freezers: 3,700.
- Current Deep Freezers: 17,280+.
- FY27 Target: 26,500+.
- Aggressive freezer rollout continues.
- Distribution is the key moat.
- Retail reach expanding rapidly.

Ice Cream Capacity
- Plant Capacity: 1,00,000 litres/day.
- Targeting 100% utilisation by Q1FY29.
- Peak Revenue Potential: ₹600 Cr.
- India's ice-cream market expected to expand significantly.
- Long-term market growth opportunity remains strong.

Management Guidance
- FY27 Revenue Growth: 50%.
- FY27 PAT Growth: 50%.
- FY29 Revenue Target: ₹1,500 Cr.
- Implied 3-year Revenue CAGR: ~73%.
- Guidance requires rigorous tracking.

Key Positives
- Strong ice-cream growth.
- Rapid distribution expansion.
- 34,000+ retail outlets.
- Massive freezer deployment.
- Significant capacity expansion.
- Multiple growth engines.
- Large addressable ice-cream market.
- Strong FY27 growth guidance.

Key Concerns
- Dry-fruit profitability needs monitoring.
- Capacity utilisation remains low.
- FY29 growth targets are ambitious.
- Ice-cream execution must continue.
- Distribution expansion requires investment.
- Margin sustainability remains important.
- Guidance execution remains key risk.

Key Monitorables
- Dry-fruit revenue growth.
- Dry-fruit EBITDA margins.
- Q2 and Q3 performance.
- Capacity utilisation.
- FY27 revenue growth.
- PAT growth.
- Freezer additions.
- Retail outlet expansion.
- Ice-cream volume growth.
- Plant utilisation.
- FY29 ₹1,500 Cr revenue target.

Investment View
- High-growth story with execution risk.
- Ice cream provides major growth opportunity.
- Dry fruits remain important for profitability.
- Distribution expansion strengthens competitive positioning.
- Capacity expansion creates significant operating leverage.
- FY29 guidance requires rigorous tracking.

Key Takeaway
- Krishival Foods is building an interesting two-engine growth story, with Melt n Mellow driving rapid ice-cream expansion while the nuts and dry-fruit business provides the established foundation. The 4x capacity expansion, aggressive freezer rollout and 34,000+ retail outlets create significant growth potential, but the key question remains whether dry-fruit profitability, capacity utilisation and ice-cream execution can support the ambitious FY27 50% growth and FY29 ₹1,500 Cr revenue target.

Astra Micro got its biggest order ever, worth 2205 crore, from HAL to make radar parts for Tejas fighter jets

This single order is bigger than all pending orders company had at end of last financial year. Company took 33 years to reach 1044 crore in yearly sales. Now management says within next 5 years, yearly sales will be 6 to 7 times higher. 

Total pending orders now stand at 4300 crore. More orders from missile defense, Su-30 radar upgrade, and electronic warfare programs are expected soon.

Astra Micro makes radar antenna units for both Indian fighter jet programs running right now. For Tejas Mk1A, it builds parts for Uttam radar which uses 912 tiny electronic modules that steer radar beams without moving parts. 

For Su-30MKI Super Sukhoi upgrade, it builds parts for Virupaksha radar using 2400 of these modules, nearly 3 times more. No other private Indian defense company works across both fighter radar programs at once. 

Combined orders from these 2 platforms can cross 5000 crore over 5 years.

Astra Micro plans to split its space and weather business into separate company called Astra Space Technologies. If you own shares, you get 1 free share of new company for every share held. Space unit made 157 crore revenue last year, around 13.5% of total sales. 

New company will start with 300 crore plus revenue and 18-20% profit margin from day 1. They plan to launch their own satellite within 6 months of listing. 
Founder S.G. Reddy leaves parent company to run this full time.

JPMORGAN ON GODREJ CONSUMER

• Rating: Overweight | Target: ₹1,175

• Surprise CEO resignation creates near-term uncertainty; CFO takes over as CEO

• Leadership transition likely to weigh on the share price in the short term

• Valuation multiples could compress until confidence in new leadership improves

• Internal succession reduces the risk of execution disruption

CITI ON GODREJ CONSUMER

• Rating: Accumulate | Target: ₹1,350

• Sudden CEO exit likely to weigh on near-term sentiment

• “Candor” and “pace” comments point to focus on transparency, accountability and faster execution

• Promoter expectations may have been higher in certain areas

• Leadership change creates a near-term overhang, but no evidence of a strategic reset

• Focus remains on improving execution within the existing strategy

MACQUARIE ON ZYDUS LIFE

• Rating: Outperform | Target: ₹1,285

• Q1 delivered an operational beat

• Management maintains FY27 guidance

• Consumer business expected to deliver double-digit growth in FY27

MACQUARIE ON HOSPITAL SECTOR 🏥

• Sees greater pricing oversight along with support for capex-intensive healthcare infrastructure

• Parliamentary committee recommendations are more interventionist than earlier policy discussions

• Report flags private healthcare as a major contributor to out-of-pocket spending and affordability concerns

• Reiterates UNDERPERFORM on Apollo Hospitals and Max Healthcare

JPMORGAN ON SIEMENS

• Rating: Underweight | Target: ₹3,334

• Margin pressure partly offset by healthy order inflows

• Q1FY27 demand remained strong with robust order inflows

• Sequential improvement in Digital Industries EBIT margin is positive

• Continued EBITDA margin compression remains the key negative

• Parliamentary committee report creates another buying opportunity

• Electricals growth driven by multiple price hikes over the last 12 months

• Communication segment margins improved on higher optical fibre cable prices and volumes

• Backward integration expected to support margins from Q3 FY27

• FMEG business continues to report positive EBIT

HSBC ON SIEMENS

• Rating: Hold | Target: ₹3,540

• Strong order inflows and execution

• Margin improvement remains elusive

• Higher input costs continue to pressure profitability

• INR depreciation also weighs on margins

INVESTEC ON ZYDUS LIFE 💊

• Rating: Sell | Target: ₹1,090 vs ₹1,000 earlier

• Zydus remains in an investment phase; payoff expected later

• US business investments continue to support the next growth phase

• Acquisitions need upfront investment before synergies materialise

• Innovation remains a key long-term growth driver

• India business growth momentum remains strong

• Target raised to ₹1,090, but rating remains Sell

- CVs face higher raw material inflation.
- Steel prices increased around 20%.
- Rubber prices saw steep increases.
- OEMs need 6–7% price hikes.
- Further hikes may not be required.
- Aluminium correction supports margin protection.
- Lower crude prices ease cost pressure.
- 4–5% price hike may be sufficient.

 **Demand Outlook**
- PV and 2W growth aided by GST cut.
- Low base also supports growth.
- EV adoption progressing without subsidies.
- Passenger EV launch pipeline remains key.

**Why read Six Faces of Globalization by Anthea Roberts & Nicolas Lamp?**

Globalization isn't just one story—it’s six competing narratives. This powerful book unpacks who wins, who loses, and why the debate matters more than ever.

**Key insights:**
 The Establishment View: Globalization drives prosperity through free markets.
🔹 The Left-Wing Critique: It widens inequality and fuels corporate power.
🔹 The Right-Wing Populist View: It undermines national identity and jobs.
🔹 The Green Perspective: Global growth endangers the planet.
🔹 Techno-Utopianism: Innovation and openness solve global problems.
🔹 Geoeconomic Realism: Nations use economics as a strategic weapon.

**Why read it?**
If you want a balanced view of globalization’s complexity, this book is your guide to understanding today’s global tug-of-war.

The Momentum Decoder: Kalyan Jewellers India Ltd (+60% in 1 month)

Kalyan Jewellers India Ltd (NSE:KALYANKJIL) surged after posting a massive 46% jump in quarterly revenue, which triggered aggressive institutional buying despite some minor margin pressure. Smart money completely absorbed the initial post-earnings profit booking near ₹568, driving a sharp volume-backed recovery that pushed the stock to finish strong at ₹610.

Bottom Line: The structural growth is impressive, but chasing a vertical 60% rally leaves no margin of safety; wait for a healthy pullback toward ₹570 before considering new entries.

Yield Spike & Global Impact 🌍

The US 30Yr Treasury yield hit 5.28%, a high unseen since 2007. The US-Iran conflict pushed WTI Crude from $67 to $115/barrel before settling near $76.

Rising crude halted the inflation decline, sparking hawkish Federal Reserve shifts. The 10Yr Treasury yield has strong support at 4.5% and could hit 5%. The Dollar Index remains firm near 98.

Tactical Play: Elevated yields strengthen the USD but crush Gold and emerging equities. Gold ($4,341) faces downside risk to $3,800. The Nifty 50 and Indian Rupee will face bearish corrections.

🎯 Bottom Line: Oil-driven inflation fears have reignited US Treasury yields. Expect a strong US Dollar, capped upside for Gold, and delayed rallies in global equities until yields decisively fall.

NUVAMA ON TITAN

Rating: HOLD (Downgraded from BUY) , Target Price: ₹5,241 (Earlier ₹5,030)

• Q1 FY27 performance was strong with revenue up 36% YoY, EBITDA up 57% and net profit up 65%

• Jewellery revenue grew 43% to ₹15,900 Cr; domestic jewellery revenue rose 38%, with like-for-like growth of 33%

• Jewellery EBIT included an inventory gain of around ₹370 Cr; MTM inventory benefit was around 75–80 bps

• CaratLane revenue grew around 41%; EBIT margin improved sharply to 11.5% from 6.6%

• International jewellery revenue jumped 136%, but the segment reported an ₹8 Cr EBIT loss amid GCC geopolitical disruptions

• Watches and eyewear businesses both grew 22%

• Nuvama expects MTM benefits to moderate over the next 2–3 quarters, while customs-duty benefits could continue for another two quarters

• Despite strong fundamentals, the recent share-price rally has reduced upside potential, prompting the downgrade to HOLD.
